analysis:
This PR adds only documentation: changelog.d/selected-models-recover.md (new, lines 1-8) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump at line 3; new selected-model-recovery paragraph at head lines 371-408). No Swift source is in the supplied batch, so the described ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift behavior cannot be verified here.

Security-relevant claims examined: (1) The recovery retry loads with allowEviction:false and may evict only non-selected, non-excluded, idle models. This is a memory-availability/DoS control (T-029, T-010 area) and does not touch the A-001 plaintext-prompt, A-003 X25519 key or attestation paths. (2) The changelog describes a policy 'pending owner review' that releases an adopted non-selected model after 10 minutes, so it takes no new requests and is evicted. This would be a new availability/fairness behavior and needs owner sign-off. It is not a confidentiality regression, and the docs do not clearly say whether it ships enabled. (3) The 'darkbloom stop/restart/start no longer need --force' and 15 s per-model unload timeout statements concern shutdown. Residual-data scrubbing after unload (T-028) could be affected if a timed-out unload lets the process exit without completing native retirement. Process exit releases memory, but this is worth confirming in code. (4) The daemon state now publishes selected_model_recovery, eviction_exclusions and serving_selection for status. These are local, model-identity-level fields that are already public via heartbeats (T-058 considered), with no stable hardware identifiers or secrets.

No T-041 prefix-cache, TTL, disk-budget or KEK changes are present. No threat-model contract (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011) is altered by these doc-only edits. Remaining question for code-bearing passes: confirm the actual recovery and eviction implementation honors in-flight, hold, pin and lease protections, and that the shutdown timeout does not skip unload cleanup.
